emergence.summary: The commonest cause of persistent neonatal hypoglycaemia, defined by inactivating mutations of the two subunits of the beta-cell ATP-sensitive potassium (K_ATP) channel: KCNJ11 (Kir6.2, the pore-forming subunit) and ABCC8 (SUR1, the sulfonylurea-receptor regulatory subunit), two ADJACENT genes on 11p15.1. The K_ATP channel couples cytosolic ATP/ADP to membrane potential: at low glucose it is OPEN (the beta-cell is hyperpolarised and insulin secretion is off); a glucose rise raises ATP, CLOSES the channel, depolarises the cell and triggers insulin release. The channel is therefore the repolarising BRAKE on glucose-stimulated insulin secretion. Loss-of-function of either subunit leaves the channel unable to open, so the beta-cell is tonically depolarised and secretes insulin INDEPENDENT of glucose -> hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia (macrosomia at birth, severe recurrent hypoglycaemia, risk of hypoglycaemic brain injury). The disease is read as the beta-cell K_ATP channel conductance axis driven DOWN (channel LOF -> the gate is stuck in the OFF basin, the repolarising K+ current is lost); the downstream consequence is unregulated insulin secretion UP. This is the cystic-fibrosis PATTERN (channel / LOF -> axis DOWN -> POTENTIATE the channel) carried onto a DIFFERENT channel and a DIFFERENT axis: where CF is an epithelial chloride-TRANSPORT channel (CFTR), this is a REGULATED-SECRETION ion channel (K_ATP / SUR1-Kir6.2) -- the kit's first regulated-hormone-secretion channel axis. It is also the kit's SIXTH two-causal-gene convergence (after HCM, sitosterolaemia, cystinuria, TSC and HHT): two subunits of ONE obligate channel, adjacent on the same chromosomal band, with KCNJ11 / Kir6.2 (the PORE) the deeper promoter switch over ABCC8 / SUR1. Correction is to POTENTIATE the channel: the K_ATP-channel opener diazoxide (Proglycem) acts on SUR1 to re-open the channel, restoring the repolarising conductance the LOF removed and curbing glucose-independent insulin release -- the approved first-line medical therapy, which the emerged switch independently re-derives. IMPORTANT HONESTY: diazoxide opens RESIDUAL / trafficking-competent channels, so the very forms most attributable to these two genes -- biallelic recessive (channel-NULL or trafficking-defective) ABCC8 / KCNJ11 disease -- are characteristically DIAZOXIDE-UNRESPONSIVE and are managed by near-total pancreatectomy (focal lesions, arising by paternal-allele loss-of-heterozygosity, can be cured by focal resection); dominant / milder K_ATP alleles are often diazoxide-responsive. So the lead lever is APPROVED but GENOTYPE-LIMITED: the corrective DIRECTION (restore K_ATP conductance) is forced [F], the realised RESPONSIVENESS / MAGNITUDE is [O] and depends on whether functional channels remain. This is the honest approved-but-partial contrast to the same release's choroideremia (a clinical-not-approved gene therapy). Somatostatin analogues (octreotide, lanreotide) and glucose-raising agents act DOWNSTREAM of the channel and are recorded as NON-levers on this switch axis; the non-channel hyperinsulinism genes (GLUD1, HADH, GCK ...) are a separate, characteristically diazoxide-RESPONSIVE class, framed as context. The gamma read is of the KCNJ11 / ABCC8 locus switch STRUCTURE (11p15.1); the disease lesions are coding (null / missense / trafficking / splice), outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].
emergence.emergent_axis: beta-cell ATP-sensitive K+ (K_ATP / SUR1-Kir6.2) channel conductance -- the repolarising brake on glucose-stimulated insulin secretion; LOF closes the gate (K+ current lost) so the beta-cell cannot repolarise -> sustained depolarisation -> voltage-gated Ca2+ influx -> unregulated insulin release (hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia). The kit's first regulated-secretion ion-channel axis, the secretory contrast to CFTR's epithelial-transport channel axis

per_gene.note: KCNJ11 encodes Kir6.2, the inward-rectifier K+ channel PORE-forming subunit of the beta-cell K_ATP channel (an octamer of four Kir6.2 + four SUR1). Inactivating (LOF) Kir6.2 mutations leave the channel unable to open, tonically depolarising the beta-cell so insulin is secreted independent of glucose -> hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia. Recessive (biallelic) LOF gives the most severe, diazoxide-unresponsive diffuse disease; dominant alleles are milder and often diazoxide-responsive. Located 11p15.1, adjacent to ABCC8. NCBI official symbol KCNJ11. The deeper promoter switch of the pair (the pore). HHF2 = OMIM 601820. Coding lesions; promoter firewall respected.
per_gene.src: Nichols 1996 Science 272:1785 (SUR1 + Kir6.2 reconstitute the beta-cell K_ATP channel; diazoxide opener); Thomas 1996 Hum Mol Genet 5:1809 (KCNJ11 in familial persistent hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia of infancy); Bellanne-Chantelot 2010 J Med Genet 47:752 (ABCC8 / KCNJ11 spectrum)

per_gene.note: ABCC8 encodes SUR1, the sulfonylurea-receptor regulatory subunit of the same K_ATP channel (the ABC-protein partner of Kir6.2; the two genes lie adjacent on 11p15.1). SUR1 confers MgADP nucleotide sensitivity and is the binding subunit for the channel-OPENER diazoxide and for sulfonylureas. LOF of SUR1 disables channel opening exactly as Kir6.2 LOF does -> the same hyperinsulinism; SUR1 is the more common cause overall. Recessive biallelic LOF -> severe, often diazoxide-unresponsive disease (diffuse, or focal via paternal-allele loss-of-heterozygosity). Located 11p15.1. NCBI official symbol ABCC8. HHF1 = OMIM 256450. Coding lesions; promoter firewall respected.
